relictum: relinquō, -ere, -līquī, -lictum — to leave behind, abandon; relictus (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
reliquit: relinquō, -ere, relīquī, relictum — to leave behind, abandon (3rd sg. perf.)
requies: requiēs, requiētis (f.) — rest, repose, respite (nom. sg.)
respicit: respiciō, -ere, -spexī, -spectum — to look back at; regard, look to (3rd sg. pres.)
ruit: ruō, -ere, ruī, rutum — to rush, hurry, fall headlong (3rd sg. pres.)
rupe: rūpēs, rūpis (f.) — cliff, crag, rock (abl. sg.)
sacrae: sacer, sacra, sacrum — holy, sacred (f. nom. pl.)
saeva: saevus, -a, -um — fierce, savage, cruel (n. acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (Gorgone saevā); n. nom./acc. pl.
saevi: saevus, -a, -um — fierce, cruel, savage (m. gen. sg.)
saevior: saevus, -a, -um — fierce, cruel (comp. saevior, f. nom. sg.: fiercer)
scilicet: scīlicet (adv.) — of course, doubtless, forsooth (often ironical)
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sedem: sēdēs, -is (f.) — seat, abode, dwelling place, site (acc. sg.)
sedens: sedeō, sedēre, sēdī, sessum — to sit (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
servat: servō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to keep, guard, preserve, watch (3rd sg. pres.)
servet: servō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to keep, save, guard (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
sibi: suī (reflexive pron.) — to/for himself, herself, themselves (dat.)
sibylla: Sibylla, -ae (f.) — the Sibyl, prophetess of Apollo at Cumae (nom. sg.)
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
simillima: similis, -e — like, similar (+ dat.); superl. simillimus (f. nom. sg.)
simulans: simulō, -āre — to imitate, pretend, feign (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
sine: sine (prep. + abl.) — without · also sinō, -ere, sīvī, situm, to allow, let (sg. imper.: sine palmula)
sinistra: sinister, -tra, -trum — left, on the left (f. abl. sg., sc. manū; also f. nom. sg.)
sonantia: sonō, -āre, sonuī, sonitum — to sound, resound (pres. part., n. acc./nom. pl.)
sonitus: sonitus, -ūs (m.) — sound, noise, clash (nom. sg.) · also nom./acc. pl. (clarescunt sonitūs) · also acc. sg.
stat: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand; be fixed (3rd sg. pres.)
strepitumque: strepitus, -ūs (m.) — din, clatter, noise (acc. sg.) + -que, and
stridor: strīdor, -ōris (m.) — hissing, creaking, crashing noise (nom. sg.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
subito: subitō (adv.) — suddenly; also subitus, -a, -um, sudden (abl./dat. sg.)
summa: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost; surface of (f. abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. nom. sg. (rēs summa; summa diēs)
super: super (adv. and prep.) — above, over; besides, in addition · also remaining, left over (sōla mei super imāgō)
superos: superī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the gods above (acc. pl.)
taedis: taeda, -ae (f.) — pine-wood, pine torch, resinous plank (abl. pl.; also dat. pl.)
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem)
tantus: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m. nom. sg.)
tartara: Tartarus, -ī (m.); pl. Tartara, -ōrum (n.) — the underworld, the nether depths (acc./nom. pl.)
telum: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, spear, arrow, weapon (acc./nom. sg.)
tempus: tempus, -oris (n.) — time, season, hour (nom. sg.) · also n. acc. sg. (tempus inane peto)
tendit: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, extend, direct one's way (3rd sg. pres.)
tenditque: tendō, tendere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, extend; to strive, aim (3rd sg. pres.) + -que 'and'
tenebat: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, grasp (3rd sg. impf.)
tenebris: tenebrae, -ārum (f. pl.) — darkness, gloom, shadows (abl./dat. pl.)
terrae: terra, -ae (f.) — earth, land, country (gen./dat. sg.; nom. pl.)
teucrum: Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — Teucrians, Trojans (gen. pl., archaic -um for -ōrum)
thalamo: thalamus, -ī (m.) — bedchamber, inner room, bridal chamber (abl./dat. sg., Greek)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
torsit: torqueō, -ēre, torsī, tortum — to twist, turn, hurl (3rd sg. perf.)
tota: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
triplici: triplex, -icis — threefold, triple (m./f./n. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
tristes: tristis, -e — sad, sorrowful, gloomy (f./m. nom. pl.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turbida: turbidus, -a, -um — stormy, turbulent, confused (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom. sg.)
turris: turris, -is (f.) — tower (acc. pl., = turrēs; also nom. sg./gen. sg.)
ulla: ūllus, -a, -um — any (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.); with non, no
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
venis: veniō, venīre, vēnī, ventum — to come (2nd sg. pres.) · also vēna, -ae (f.) — vein, blood-vessel (abl. pl.: volnus alit venis)
venit: veniō, venīre, vēnī — to come (3rd sg. perf. vēnit, or pres. venit)
veterum: vetus, veteris — old, ancient, long-standing (gen. pl.)
vicissim: vicissim (adv.) — in turn, in succession, on the other hand
videt: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. pres.)
vidi: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (1st sg. perf.)
virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
vis: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, power, violence; pl. vīrēs, strength (nom. sg.)
viscera: viscus, vīsceris (n.) — flesh; pl. viscera, entrails (acc. pl.)
vocabat: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, summon, invite (3rd sg. imperf.)
vocat: vocō, -āre — to call, name, summon (3rd sg. pres.)
volvuntur: volvō, -ere, volvī, volūtum — to roll; pass. roll, flow (3rd pl. pres. pass.)
